newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies lower.

text.p: CME hog futures ended mixed as profit-taking offset stronger fundamentals, while pork belly futures finished lower on concern over product going into storage, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.150 cent per lb higher to 0.250 lower with June up most at 85.000 cents. July posted a new contract high of 86.650 before ending unchanged. Pork bellies finished 0.975 to 2.275 lower with July off 1.475 at 90.100 cents.
Profit-taking and unwinding of spreads weighed on hog futures despite continued support from firm cash ideas, traders said.

Long fund rolling lifted July to a new high before the unwinding of bear spreads by commission houses and the profit-taking developed. Commercial buying boosted futures at times, reflecting expectations of steady to firmer cash hog markets again Monday and recent gains in cash pork products, they said.
However, cash pork prices showed an uneven tone at noon and futures slipped before fund buying provided support at the close, they added.

Rand Financials bought June early while selling August. Lind-Waldock and RBH bought June and sold August late. Cargill Investor Services sold June while locals bought. Locals and Lind-Waldock sold July, pit sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock bought October 80 and 82 calls while Refco bought December 74 puts and October 76 puts. Cargill sold deep in the money October 60 to 64 calls, pit sources added.
Pork bellies pared losses late on local short-covering but remained pressured by commercial and mixed commission house selling prompted by concern over storings, traders said.

Reports that increased amounts of product were going into frozen storage prompted liquidation in futures and prices declined into sell stops. Higher futures prices recently attracted warehouse storing interest, they said.
"You have a good basis to store," one trader said.

However, underlying support continued to stem from the slow hog slaughter pace. Hog slaughter year to date is down 6.3 percent from last year's pace. It may be hard to store any significant amount of bellies if production remains light, they added.
Rand Financials, Refco and Rosenthal Collins sold July down into stops before locals covered. LFG bought early, pit sources said.
